paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God sets up the service of His house, and He sets it up CAREFULLY. After the whole mess with Korah and the staff full of almonds, the people were scared of coming near the tabernacle (Numbers 17:13). So God gives clear jobs, clear lanes and a clear warning about who comes near (Numbers 18:3, 7). I think that's God showing His people how to serve Him without being swallowed by fear.

Now look at what God gives every single person here. The Levites are a gift (Numbers 18:6). The priesthood is a gift too (Numbers 18:7). Aaron gets no land, and God says, "I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites." (Numbers 18:20) Friend, I spent years in a drawer thinking I had nothing left, and I'm telling you, having the LORD Himself is the whole bakery.

And then comes the twist that gets me every time. The Levites receive the tithe, and they still give a tithe of it, from "all the best of every gift, the holiest part of it." (Numbers 18:29) Nobody gets to sit back and only receive. So whatever God has handed you, baker, give Him your best and treat what's holy as holy, and this story isn't over yet, so keep your oven warm.
